exampleAnswers.title: Identifying the Vertical Shift of a Transformed Secant or Cosecant Curve

question.text: The graph above shows the function $y = \sec\left(\dfrac{3x}{4}\right) + D,$ where $D$ is a constant. What is the value of $D?$
question.explanation:
The constant $D$ represents a vertical shift of the function $y = \sec\left(\dfrac{3x}{4}\right).$

Since the local minimum of secant is $y = 1,$ from the graph we see that the given curve is shifted up by $4-1=3$ units. So, the equation of the curve is \[ y = \sec\left(\dfrac{3x}{4}\right) + 3. \]

Therefore, $D = 3.$

exampleAnswers.title: Identifying the Horizontal Shift of a Transformed Secant or Cosecant Curve

question.text: The graph above shows a section of the function $y=\dfrac{1}{2}\sec{(x+C)},$ where $C$ is a constant. Given that $-\pi < C < \pi,$ what is the value of $C?$
question.explanation:
The constant $C$ represents a horizontal shift of the function $y=\dfrac{1}{2}\sec x.$

From the graph, we see that the given curve is a secant graph that's been shifted left by $2$ units. So, the equation of the curve is:

\[ y=\dfrac{1}{2}\sec\left(x+2\right) \]

Therefore, $C =2.$

question.text: The graph above shows a section of the function $y=\dfrac{3}{2}\sec{(x+C)},$ where $C$ is a constant. Given that $-\pi < C < \pi,$ what is the value of $C?$
question.explanation:
The constant $C$ represents a horizontal shift of the function $y=\dfrac{3}{2}\sec x.$

From the graph, we see that the given curve is a secant graph that's been shifted right by $\dfrac {\pi} 4$ units. So, the equation of the curve is:

\[ y=\dfrac{3}{2}\sec\left(x-\frac {\pi} 4\right) \]

Therefore, $C =-\dfrac {\pi} 4.$

exampleAnswers.title: Identifying the Horizontal Stretch of a Transformed Secant or Cosecant Curve

question.text: The graph above shows the function $y=\csc{\left(Bx\right)}+3,$ where $B$ is a constant. What is the value of $B?$
question.explanation:
The period $T$ of the function is:

\[ T = \frac{5\pi}{2} -0 = \dfrac{5\pi}{2}. \]

The formula for the period $T$ of the function $y=A\csc(Bx + C) + D$ is given by

\[ T = \dfrac{2\pi}{B}. \]

Applying the formula of the period, we get:

\[ \dfrac{5\pi}{2} = \dfrac{2\pi}{B}\quad\Longrightarrow\quad B = \dfrac{2\pi}{\left(\dfrac{5\pi}{2}\right)} = \dfrac{4}{5} \]

Finally, the equation of the curve is:

\[ y=\csc\left( \dfrac{4}{5}x\right)+3 \]

example.title: Identifying the Horizontal Stretch of a Transformed Secant or Cosecant Curve

question.text: The graph above shows the function $y = \csc(Bx) + \dfrac{1}{2},$ where $B$ is a constant. What is the value of $B?$
question.explanation:
The period $T$ of the function is \[ T = \dfrac{\pi}{2} - \left(-\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right) = \pi. \]

The formula for the period $T$ of the function $y = A\csc(Bx + C) + D$ is given by \[ T = \dfrac{2\pi}{B}. \]

Applying the formula of the period, we get \[ \pi = \dfrac{2\pi}{B} \quad\Longrightarrow\quad B = \dfrac{2\pi}{\pi} = 2. \]

Finally, the equation of the curve is \[ y = \csc(2x) + \dfrac{1}{2}. \]

exampleAnswers.title: Identifying the Horizontal Stretch and Vertical Shift of a Transformed Secant or Cosecant Curve

question.text: The graph above shows the function $y=\csc{(Bx)}+D,$ where $B$ and $D$ are constants. What is $B+D?$
question.explanation:
The period $T$ of the function is $6\pi.$

The formula for the period $T$ of the function $y=A\csc(Bx + C) + D$ is given by

\[ T = \dfrac{2\pi}{B} \]

Applying the formula of the period, we get:

\[ 6\pi = \dfrac{2\pi}{B}\quad\Longrightarrow\quad B = \dfrac{2\pi}{6\pi} = \dfrac{1}{3} \]

The parameter $D$ represents the vertical shift of the cosecant function. Since the local minimum of cosecant is $y=1$, we see that the function has been translated by $3$ units down. Hence, $D=-3.$

Therefore, $B+D = \dfrac 1 3 -3 = -\dfrac 8 3.$

Finally, the equation of the curve is:

\[ y=\csc\left(\frac{x}{3}\right)-3 \]

example.title: Identifying the Horizontal Stretch and Vertical Shift of a Transformed Secant or Cosecant Curve

question.text: The graph above shows the function $y=\sec{(Bx)}+D,$ where $B$ and $D$ are constants. What is $B+D?$
question.explanation:
The period $T$ of the function is \[ 3\pi-\left(-\pi\right)=4\pi. \]

The formula for the period $T$ of the function $y=A\sec(Bx + C) + D$ is given by

\[ T = \dfrac{2\pi}{B}. \]

Applying the formula of the period, we get:

\[ 4\pi = \dfrac{2\pi}{B}\quad\Longrightarrow\quad B = \dfrac{2\pi}{4\pi} = \dfrac{1}{2} \]

The parameter $D$ represents the vertical shift of the secant function. Since the local minimum of secant is $y=1$, we see that the function has been translated by $2$ units up. Hence, $D=2.$

Therefore, $B+D = \dfrac 1 2 +2 = \dfrac{5}{2}.$

Finally, the equation of the curve is:

\[ y=\sec\left(\frac{x}{2}\right)+2 \]

exampleAnswers.title: Identifying the Horizontal Shift of a Horizontally Stretched Secant or Cosecant Curve

question.text: The graph above shows the function $y = \csc\left(\dfrac{4x}{5} + C\right),$ where $C$ is a constant. Given that $-\pi < C < \pi,$ what is the value of $C?$
question.explanation:
The parameter $C$ represents a horizontal shift of the function.

First, we rewrite the function by factoring the horizontal stretch factor, as follows: \begin{align*} y & =\csc\left(\dfrac{4x}{5} + C\right)\\[5pt] & = \csc\left(\dfrac{4}{5}\left(x + \dfrac{5C}{4} \right)\right) \end{align*}

From the graph, we see that the graph of cosecant has been shifted by $\dfrac{7\pi}{8}$ units to the right. Therefore \[ \dfrac{5C}{4} = -\dfrac{7\pi}{8} \quad \Longrightarrow\quad C = -\dfrac{7\pi}{10}. \]

example.title: Identifying the Horizontal Shift of a Horizontally Stretched Secant or Cosecant Curve

question.text: The graph above shows the function $y=\sec{\left(\dfrac{x}{4}+C\right)},$ where $C$ is a constant. Given that $-\pi < C < \pi,$ what is the value of $C?$
question.explanation:
The parameter $C$ represents a horizontal shift of the function.

First, we rewrite the function by factoring the horizontal stretch factor, as follows:

\begin{align*} y & =\sec{\left(\dfrac{x}{4}+C\right)}\\[5pt] & =\sec{\left(\dfrac{1}{4}\left(x+4C\right)\right)}\\[5pt] \end{align*}

From the graph, we see that the graph of secant has been shifted by $\dfrac{4\pi}{3}$ units to the left. Therefore:

\[ 4C = \dfrac{4\pi}{3}\quad\Longrightarrow\quad C = \dfrac \pi 3 \]
